target_customer: Trucking carriers and freight brokers buying and bidding on spot loads
problem: Spot freight opportunities are scattered across shipper portals and email, causing empty miles and slow bidding.

competitors.name: Convoy Platform (Flexport)
competitors.what: Load board for carriers and brokers revived from the shuttered Convoy's technology, with book-at-rate and bid options
competitors.traction_then: Launched about four months after Flexport bought Convoy's IP in Nov 2023; no usage figures

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating loads from many portals and email requires many integrations and parsing; standard engineering with messy inputs.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and bid rules create some workflow lock-in; no proprietary data evidence.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Load-board incumbents and Flexport's revived Convoy platform covered adjacent ground in 2024; no report of any of them copying or buying Manifold. Manifold stayed independent and reported as alive in 2025-2026 listings.

market_need_then: Convoy's Oct 2023 collapse left carriers without a spot-freight channel; GeekWire (May 2024) frames spot freight as scattered one-off loads across brokers, and the YC launch post claims $5,100 monthly revenue two months after launch (company-reported).

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: A Better Way to Win Freight

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no source on the name's meaning, logo or community; the word 'Manifold' is generic and shared with other companies. Only product and funding coverage exists.

pivots.to: Pricing strategy and automation platform for brokers and carriers (AI assistants Manny and Console)
pivots.why: Not stated; undated, based on current site

outcome_analysis: Manifold Freight was founded in Seattle by two early Convoy engineers (employees #12 and #50) in YC W24 and raised a $1.9M seed in May 2024 led by New Stack Ventures and YC, while Convoy's collapse in October 2023 and Flexport's revival of its load board shaped the market. It remains listed Active with 2-10 employees; its domain moved to getmanifold.ai and the site now stresses pricing automation and AI agents, an undated broadening of scope. No exit or later round is public, so it reads as an early company with founder-market fit and unproven traction.
notes: Searches done: outcome (no shutdown or acquisition found), funding, funding cross-check (two GeekWire headlines, Startup Intros and CB Insights; GeekWire pages returned 403 on fetch, so details come from search summaries), dated competitor (Convoy collapse and Flexport relaunch), branding. Seed $1.9M (May 2024) consistent across GeekWire and aggregators; an earlier GeekWire piece mentions $500K from YC (not recorded; YC standard deal) and aggregators show a $2.4M total across two rounds (unverified). Competitor source_date given only as 2024 because the FreightWaves article's exact date was not seen; relaunch described as almost four months after the Nov 2023 acquisition. DAT and Truckstop load boards existed but no source dated near the batch was found, so not listed. Pivot (pricing automation, AI assistants) is undated, based on the current site.
